title: Struggling to find or create a shootdodge animation like Max Payne 3. Any advice?
author: Faisal_alwaal
selftext:
Hey guys,

I'm working on a third-person shooter and I've been trying to add a shootdodge mechanic similar to Max Payne 3.

I looked through Fab hoping to find an animation pack I could buy, but I couldn't find anything that really resembles Max Payne's shootdodge.

I also tried getting Claude to create the animations. I gave it multiple references and even recorded my own Max Payne 3 gameplay to show exactly how the movement should look, but the results were nowhere near what I wanted. I tried Kimodo as well, but didn't have much luck with that either.

I'm honestly not sure what to do at this point. Is a proper shootdodge animation really that difficult to make, or am I just approaching it the wrong way?

Has anyone here managed to implement something similar? I'd love to know how you did it.

Also, if anyone knows of an animation pack or asset that has a decent shootdodge, please share a link. I'd be more than happy to buy it.

Any advice would be appreciated.

comments.author: HouseOfWyrd
comments.body:
Just for context, you're asking an AI to try and create an animation based on what is a complex physics based animation system.

You're not going to be able to just go "make this" - you'll need more understanding of how such a thing works and then step through that with the AI.

replies.author: HardSellStudios
replies.body: 100% this. The quality you get reflects your own ability to understand and define what you want, and to guide the AI to the result. The AI can help you better understand it though so there is also a great learning opportunity here as well. ​

replies.author: LiteratureSelect4478
replies.body:
This   1000%

I mean I don't know everything right but I know what I want.  So I'll go research it with chatgpt as its pretty quick, I tell it what im thinking about and what game im working on as in engine etc let it know where im at - might even upload the src code so it can read through it   - then spend the next 30 mins back and forth talking about what it found and i found, ask it to send links - go watch them, click around for more info as you'll get an understanding to start deeper digging - do it with chaggpt and post more back and forth. Then ask it condense everything into file and make hand off plan.  Throw that plan and chat Into claude with your src code as well and it will see if it is all feasible and then offer suggestions and plan it better than chatgpt.  More back and forth and boom a ratified plan to get a feature into your game safely and on track with little deviation.

Your new system has been ratified and thought about with your game In mind and now is planned to start putting it in


Ive like 30 handoff logs well drilled ready to implement.   Even ai in whatsapp isn't bad for spitballing ideas when your sitting on the toilet and thinking  - can my game support better graphics,physics,fog etc and you go through the whole dance again   

Saves me soo much random searches like- what's the best shades for my game engine.  Etc

Or id see some tech being demonstrated in a game, go research how they did it - go through the same process. By this stage I get told my own engine already does it and tells me how to tweak it - that's the next stage as its not going to tell you that unless you ask about it.  Which is fine. I do accuse it as being g a gatekeeper lol but if I understood more it will answer those questions  - it just won't hand them to me and will do what its told and not go hey BTW you can also do a b c d e f g now   

Add Pictures along the way in the dicussion.   It's like telling a gifted kid how you want something to come out - you don't tell it how to get there with too much input if you have planned it well.   As you have already smashed it and now coding to see the results only now

The benefit ive seen with this approach is ill tell opus 5.5 to delegate to cheaper models and check the work and its saved me massively and can get a lot more done than just letting opus do it -  even letting fable plan it was better.  Same then again tell opus to delegate. If its well drilled plan cheap models eat it for breakfast for bugger all tokens used.  I wow dropped a sub cos of it. Don't need it

comments.author: NoBackupDev
comments.body:
There are motion to animation tools that can animate a rig from a video. You can try those.

Otherwise, I would consider pivoting to a more whimsy cartoonish style where realism is less important.

comments.author: Xinnobun
comments.body: Apparently there were 1100\~ people who worked on creating max payne 3, you're trying to do it with 1 person and AI. You will have to accept certain limitations.

replies.author: Faisal_alwaal
replies.body:
Believe it or not, a lot of things I thought would be difficult turned out to be much easier than I expected. Unreal Engine has honestly been a blessing and made so many things possible.

Funny enough, the things I thought would be easy, like the shootdodge and cover system, turned out to be way more complicated than I imagined.

At least with the cover system, there are tons of ready-made packages on Fab, so you can take a shortcut if you want. But the shootdodge? That's been a real headache. I genuinely didn't expect it to be this difficult to get right.
